title: Tenant proportional holdback and soft-spill routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a tenant-aware proportional holdback admission layer plus a soft-spill routing policy to reduce hard rejects during transient overloads on Dedicated fleets. The goal is to provide predictable minimum throughput guarantees for contracted tenants while preserving fleet utilization and minimizing user-facing latency and errors. This ticket covers admission calculus, token reservation semantics, spill routing to best-effort lanes, and autoscaler integration for headroom signals.
acceptance_criteria: Admission controller enforces per-tenant proportional holdback (%) derived from reservation contracts and recent usage without causing starvation for bursty tenants
Soft-spill routing routes excess requests to best-effort lanes (lower priority pools) when headroom exhausted, with fallbacks to hosted models or queued deferment rather than immediate 429s
End-to-end integration with autoscaler: holdback respects predicted scale-up time and autoscaler intent so we avoid oscillation and unnecessary shedding
System metrics added: holdback_allocated, holdback_used, soft_spill_count, avg_spill_latency, queue_wait_p50/p95, per-tenant_reject_rate
Simulation shows <=1% sovereign SLA regressions for guaranteed tenants and reduces hard rejects by >=70% during 2x sudden load spikes in synthetic workloads
Documentation and runbook for operators including knob defaults, failure modes, and migration steps to enable per-tenant reservations
comments: 2026-02-16 Aisha: Initial scoping — defined proportional holdback as a fraction of contracted throughput + minimum floor. Decided to model holdback as a time-windowed token reservation rather than static rate to allow short bursts.

2026-02-19 Luca: Design review notes — prefer soft-spill over blind queueing for tenant UX; recommended adding platform-level fallback to hosted API for customers with hybrid routing enabled. Action: prototype routing shim that tags requests with spill_reason and originating_tier.

2026-02-23 Infra sim: Ran kilo-agent simulator with 100 tenants (mix reserved/unreserved). Results: hard-429s reduced by 73% when soft-spill enabled; tail latency for priority tenants increased by 7ms median, +22ms p95 in the worst case. Recorded artifacts in Confluence.

2026-02-25 Design: UX input from Sarah (Console PM) — include per-tenant holdback visualization and spill log in Console. Added label: observability-needed. PM asked for clear opt-out for spill routing per-customer.

2026-02-28 Security: Karthik notes — ensure spill metadata does not leak internal tenant allocation details to other tenants or logs. Will redact tenant contract IDs and surface only tenant-visible names in customer-facing logs.

2026-03-02 Dev update: Implemented admission token allocator and basic soft-spill router. Endpoints: /admission/eval and /admission/commit. Unit tests cover token expiry and concurrent allocation edge cases. Open PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rw-admission/pull/241

2026-03-04 Load test: Canary on dedicated-staging: enabled holdback for 3 reserved customers. Observed autoscaler spin-up for fleet +1 node after sustained 20% headroom deficit within 90s — matches autoscaler intent. Noted minor oscillation when tenant burst TTL is very short; mitigation: add adaptive backoff window per-tenant.
2026-03-05 PM check-in: Luca and Aisha synced with Support on migration messaging. Ops runbook draft attached. Next: add tracing hooks and integrate with console dashboard before review.

Review feedback: PR reviewers asked for clearer invariants around reservation decay and a design doc section on fairness when multiple reserved tenants exceed combined guarantees. Added simulation plan to exercise adversarial scenarios.
notes: Key trade-offs: conservative holdback values keep guarantees but reduce absorbable burst capacity; aggressive soft-spill improves UX but may increase tail latency on best-effort pools. We prefer conservative defaults with opt-in higher utilization modes. Plan phased rollout: internal-only -> beta customers -> GA.
runbook_summary: If customers see unexpected rejections: check holdback_allocated vs holdback_used, inspect soft_spill_count and queue_wait_p95. Common fixes: increase reserved holdback, widen autoscaler headroom, or enable temporary hosted fallback.
migration_plan: 1) Add telemetry + feature flag in Dedicated control plane. 2) Enable for internal tenants only. 3) Run 2 weeks of canary with synthetic spikes. 4) Enable beta for opt-in customers. 5) Gradual default enable after 4-week observation window.
